blocks.text: אַאְפִּיד נֵזֶר אָיוֹם. בְּשִׁלּוּשׁ קְדֻשָּׁה כַּיּוֹם: גִּבּוֹרֵי כֹחַ גְּדֻלָּה. דַּהֲרוּהוּ בְּבֵית דְּגִילָה: הוֹגֵי הֶגֶה הֲמֻלָּה. וַתְּקוּהוּ בְּהַלֵּל וּמִלָּה: זוֹכֵר לָעַד זָכִיּוֹת. חַדְּשׁוּהוּ זֶמֶר חַיּוֹת: טוֹב, עוֹמֵס מְרַח. יַחֲדוּהוּ בְּחִדּוּשׁ יָרֵחַ: כּוֹבֵשׁ כָּל־כְּעָסִים. לְבַל אַף לְהָשִׂים: מְשָׁרְתֵי בְּחִיל מוֹרָא. נָכְחָם הַלְּלוּ נוֹרָא: שַׂרְפֵי סְבִיב סְעָרָה. עֱנוּ לְמַעֲבִיר
uncertainties: The stanza breaks off mid-sentence at לְמַעֲבִיר at the foot of the upper section. It continues on a later page.
נֵזֶר: the first vowel could be tsere or segol.
כֹחַ: I can't tell whether the כ has a dagesh.
וַתְּקוּהוּ: the pointing is unclear. It could also be וַתְּקָוּהוּ.
זָכִיּוֹת: there is a small vertical stroke near the ז, possibly a meteg.
מְרַח: the vowel under the מ could be sheva or segol (מֶרַח).
יָרֵחַ: there is a vertical stroke under the ר, possibly a meteg or an accent.
מְשָׁרְתֵי: I read final יּ with tsere under the ת. The image does not clearly show משרתיו.
נָכְחָם: the first vowel could be qamats or patah.
Comma after טוֹב, as printed.

blocks.text: ח׳ מטת צָרִים שַׁבֵּר וְהַכְחִידֵם. זְרוּיֶיךָ קַבֵּץ וְחִנָּם תִּפְדֵּם. ק׳ זְכוֹר עֲדָתְךָ קָנִיתָ קֶּדֶם: ח׳ נְדִיבֵי עַמִּים יְנַחֲמוּ בְּכִפְלַיִם. קָמֵיהֶם עַל פְּנֵימוֹ גַּלֵּה שׁוּלַיִם. ק׳ זְכֹר יְיָ לִבְנֵי אֱדוֹם אֵת יוֹם יְרוּשָׁלָםִ: ח׳ סַלּוּל מְסִלָּתֵנוּ יַשֵּׁר לִצְעוֹד. וּבֵין יְקִירְךָ קַרְסֹל לֹא יִמְעוֹד. ק׳ כְּנַמְתָּ זָכוֹר אֶזְכְּרֶנּוּ עוֹד:
uncertainties: Speaker sigla are inline: ח׳ = chazzan, ק׳ = congregation (kahal).
The opening word מטת seems to be printed without vowels.
קֶּדֶם: I can't tell whether the ק has a dagesh. If it is printed, it is a likely typo for קֶדֶם.
יְנַחֲמוּ: the first vowels are unclear. It could be יֶנֱחָמוּ.
סַלּוּל: the first vowel and dagesh are unclear. It could be סְלוּל or סָלוּל.
יְקִירְךָ: the pointing on the yod and resh is unclear.
פְּנֵימוֹ: the vowel under the פ could be sheva or qamats.
The ק׳ lines are biblical quotations (Ps 74:2; Ps 137:7; Jer 31:19). I see no cantillation marks on them.

blocks.text: שְׁבוּתֵינוּ.
uncertainties: Small type set apart at the end of the זכור אזכרנו עוד line. It seems to be a cue word or catchword rather than part of the stanza. Please confirm what it does.

blocks.text: ח׳ קִרְיַת מָשׂוֹשׂ הֵיכָל וְאוּלָם. מִזְבֵּחַ יָשִׁיב וּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת כֻּלָּם. ק׳ יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ לְעוֹלָם: ח׳ שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ יְרַנְּנוּ לִשְׁמוֹ. יְעָרוֹת יִמְחֲאוּ כַף לְהַנְעִימוֹ. ק׳ כִּי פָקַד יְיָ אֶת עַמּוֹ: ח׳ תְּקֶף אֶרְאֶלִּים וְכוֹכְבֵי צְפַר. תְּהִלּוֹת יִתְּנוּ שֶׁבַח לְהַשְׁפַּר. ק׳ הַלְלוּהוּ בְּתֵקַע שׁוֹפָר:
uncertainties: There is a mark under the ז of מִזְבֵּחַ, possibly a meteg.
לְעוֹלָם is printed plene. Exodus 15:18 has defective לְעֹלָם.
תְּקֶף: the first vowel could be sheva or holam (תֹּקֶף).
The ק׳ lines are biblical quotations (Ex 15:18; Ruth 1:6; Ps 150:3).

blocks.text: (כָּל יוֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל וְשׁוֹכְנֵי אָרֶץ. יֹאמְרוּ תָמִיד הִגְדִּיל יְיָ לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּאָרֶץ. וְהָיָה יְיָ לְמֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ. קָדוֹשׁ:)
uncertainties: Set in smaller type, indented and in parentheses. The parentheses are printed.

blocks.text: ח״ק יִשְׁפֹּט תֵּבֵל בְּצֶדֶק וּלְאֻמִּים בְּמֵישָׁרִים. הָאֵל קָדוֹשׁ:
uncertainties: ח״ק = chazzan and congregation. It is a speaker siglum.

blocks.text: ח״ק וְהוּא בְּאֶחָד וּמִי יְשִׁיבֶנּוּ. וְנַפְשׁוֹ אִוְּתָה וַיָּעַשׂ. נוֹרָא וְקָדוֹשׁ:
uncertainties: This quotes Job 23:13. There is a vertical stroke under the י of וַיָּעַשׂ, which may be a meteg or a cantillation accent. I see no other cantillation on the line.
בְּאֶחָד: the ב seems to have a dagesh and sheva. The Masoretic text has בְאֶחָד.
אִוְּתָה: I can't tell whether the ו has a dagesh.

blocks.text: Morning Prayer for the New Year
אאפיד

I adorn the awe-inspiring with a crown through the threefold sanctification of the day. The strong in might and greatness rejoice before Him in the house of assembly. They who praise in tumultuous throngs, laud Him with glorifying word. To Him who remembers piety for ever, do the Hayoth sing a new song. Praise Him alone — benevolent is He and forgives sins — on the day of the new moon. He suppresses wrath entirely and does not allow anger. O you (the angels) who serve Him in trembling and fear, praise Him who is awe-inspiring in the presence of those (Israel). Angels of fire encircled by the whirlwind, chant in honour of Him who
uncertainties: The text breaks off mid-sentence at 'who', matching the Hebrew page.
There is a stray macron-like mark over the 'i' of 'sing' (printed 'sīng'). It is probably a print or scan artifact. Proposed reading: 'sing'.

blocks.text: On Sabbath.
uncertainties: Printed in italics.

blocks.text: מטת

Break the yoke of adversaries, destroy them; gather those dispersed by Thee and redeem them without ransom. Remember Thy congregation which Thou hast once chosen. Comfort the noblest of peoples, expose to their faces the shame of those who rise against them; remember, O Lord, against the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem. Make even our highway, straighten it for our steps that the foot of Thy favourite may not stumble, as Thou hast said: I will surely still remember him.
uncertainties: The English does not translate the Hebrew catchword שְׁבוּתֵינוּ.

blocks.text: קרית

The joyful city, sanctum and porch, and the altar may He restore with all the sacred vessels; the Lord will reign for ever. Heaven and earth exult at His Name; forests clap their hands in delight in Him; for the Lord has considered His people. The mighty Erelim and the bright stars in glory will proclaim His praise. Praise Him with the Shofar blast.
(כל
uncertainties: The opening parenthesis comes before the Hebrew cue word.

blocks.text: All the inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth do constantly say: Great things has the Lord performed on earth, and the Lord shall be King over all the earth, the Holy One.)
uncertainties: The opening parenthesis is attached to the linkage cue and the closing one ends this passage.

blocks.text: ישפט
He judges the world in justice and nations in righteousness, God is holy.
uncertainties: 'right-eousness' is hyphenated across a line break. I have joined it.

blocks.text: והוא
He is unique, who can reply to Him? Whatever His soul desires, He accomplishes, Awe-inspiring and Holy!

notes: s138 and s139 were read as whole pages, as assigned. On both, a horizontal rule separates the continuation of the main קרובות stanza (אאפיד, an alphabetical acrostic marked ע״ס א״ב) from the Sabbath-only insertion (מטת … / קרית …) below it. The Sabbath section is a printed conditional alternative.

Recitation roles below the rule on s138: ח׳ (chazzan) alternates with ק׳ (kahal/congregation), which recites biblical verses. ח״ק (chazzan and congregation together) introduces ישפט and והוא. The English page has no speaker sigla.
The Hebrew rubric below the rule (read as חַזָּן שַׁבָּת.) is uncertain. It matches 'On Sabbath.' on the English page. Please check it against the original.
שְׁבוּתֵינוּ at the end of the מטת stanza is in small type and has no English counterpart. I took it as a cue word or catchword rather than prayer text.
I saw no Biblical cantillation apart from a possible accent under the י of וַיָּעַשׂ (Job 23:13). Vertical strokes elsewhere seem to be metegs and are listed per block.
Overlapping band regions were checked against the full pages, and no lines are duplicated.
